meta.name: Heart2Heart Foundation
meta.description: Compassionate, confidential counselling and therapeutic support for secondary-school girls and married women.

emergency.title: Need help now?
emergency.lede: If you are in immediate danger, or you are worried about your safety or someone else's, please reach out straight away. You do not have to explain everything to get help.
emergency.contactsNote: The Foundation checks and re-confirms every number on this page. If a number does not connect, please tell us so we can correct it.
emergency.urgentRequestNote: Send a short message to the Foundation. A member of the team responds during working hours — this is not a 24-hour service.
emergency.notEmergencyService: Heart2Heart Foundation is not an emergency service and does not operate around the clock. In a life-threatening emergency, please contact the police or the nearest hospital.
emergency.privacyTipBody: Anyone who uses this device may be able to see the pages you visited. You can use a private or incognito window, and clear your history afterwards.

home.heroTitle: A safe place to talk, whenever you are ready.
home.heroBody: Heart2Heart Foundation offers confidential counselling and therapeutic support for secondary-school girls and married women — with no judgement, and at your pace.
home.heroAssurance: Private · Free to ask · You choose how we reply
home.whoBody: Two groups, two different kinds of pressure. Both deserve someone who listens properly.
home.servicesBody: Everything the Foundation offers is supervised by a qualified professional.
home.howBody: Four steps, and you can stop at any point.

one.title: Tell us a little
one.body: A short private form. Use any name you like — you do not have to give your real one.

two.title: We review it
two.body: A qualified therapist reads your request. Nobody else sees it.

three.title: We agree a time
three.body: We contact you the way you asked us to, and find a time that works.

four.title: You talk
four.body: A confidential session, plus follow-up or a referral if that would help.

home.privacyTitle: What you tell us stays private
home.privacyBody: Counselling information is never treated like ordinary website content. Your request is only visible to the Foundation's authorised counselling staff — never to visitors, donors or volunteers.
privacyPoints: You can use a preferred name instead of your real one.
You choose how we contact you, and when.
Your request is stored separately from the public website.
You can ask us to delete your information at any time.
home.resourcesBody: Articles, videos and guides you can go through in your own time.
home.eventsBody: Outreach, workshops and awareness programmes across the community.
home.donateBody: Every session the Foundation provides is funded by people who believe girls and women deserve somewhere to turn. A gift of any size keeps the door open.
home.ctaTitle: You don't have to work it out alone.
home.ctaBody: Starting the conversation takes a few minutes, and you decide what happens next.

about.title: About the Foundation
about.lede: Heart2Heart Foundation exists so that girls and women in our community have somewhere trustworthy to turn when life becomes difficult.
about.mission: To provide accessible and compassionate counselling, and therapeutic support for secondary-school girls and married women, helping them build emotional wellbeing, resilience, and healthier lives.
about.vision: To build a trusted support ecosystem where women and girls can access appropriate counselling, education, guidance, referrals, and support in a safe, respectful, and confidential environment.
about.problemBody: Many women and girls experiencing emotional, relationship, family, marital or social difficulties do not have access to an appropriate and trusted place to seek help. The reasons are rarely simple.
about.barriersTitle: The barriers we hear about most
barriers: Not knowing this kind of support exists
No confidential channel to talk through
Few educational resources in plain language
about.approachBody: Professional counselling, therapeutic support, education, awareness programmes, community outreach and appropriate referrals — delivered with respect for privacy at every step.

values.title: Confidentiality first
values.body: Private counselling data is never treated like ordinary website content, and it never appears anywhere a visitor can reach.

values.title: Professional supervision
values.body: Support areas and clinical decisions are determined and supervised by qualified professionals.

values.title: No judgement
values.body: People come to us at difficult moments. Our job is to listen properly, not to assess how they got there.

values.title: Know our limits
values.body: When someone needs specialist care we say so, and we refer them onward rather than holding on.

about.teamBody: The Foundation currently works with one qualified therapist, supported by trained volunteers and administrative staff. The platform is built so additional therapists can join without disruption.
about.safeguardingBody: Because the Foundation supports women and, in some cases, minors, safeguarding sits at the centre of how we work.

services.title: Counselling and support services
services.lede: Support is shaped around who you are and what you are carrying. Specific services are determined and supervised by qualified professionals.
services.girlsBody: School years bring pressures that are easy for adults to underestimate. You can talk about any of these — or something not on this list.
services.womenBody: Marriage and family life can be hard to talk about honestly with the people closest to you. This is a space where you can.

how.title: One-to-one counselling
how.body: A confidential conversation with a qualified therapist, in person or by phone, at a time you agreed in advance.

how.title: Follow-up
how.body: If it would help, we arrange further sessions. Nothing is decided without you.

how.title: Referral
how.body: Where specialist care is the right answer, we connect you with an appropriate professional or organisation.

how.title: Education and awareness
how.body: Workshops, school outreach and resources that make these conversations easier to have.

services.limitsBody: The Foundation is not an emergency service and cannot provide 24-hour crisis response, medical treatment or legal representation. If you are in immediate danger, please use the emergency page.

counselling.girlCardBody: Support with school pressure, friendships, family, bullying, confidence and anything else on your mind.
counselling.womanCardBody: Support with marriage, family pressure, communication, emotional wellbeing and difficult home situations.

fields.ageRangeHint: This helps the therapist prepare, and tells us which safeguarding steps apply.
fields.supportAreas: What would you like support with?

fields.reasonHint: A sentence or two is enough. You do not need to write everything down now — the session is where you can talk properly.
fields.reasonPlaceholder: For example: I've been feeling low for a few months and I don't have anyone to talk to about it.
fields.contactMethodHint: Choose whatever is safest and most private for you.

fields.contactValueHintEmail: An email address you check privately.

fields.contactNotes: Anything we should know about contacting you
fields.contactNotesPlaceholder: For example: please only call in the afternoon.
fields.preferredDateHint: We'll do our best. If it isn't possible, we'll suggest another time.
fields.guardianAware: Does a parent or guardian know you are asking for support?

fields.safetyQuestion: Are you currently worried about your immediate safety?
fields.safetyQuestionHint: If yes, we will treat your request as urgent. If you are in danger right now, please use the emergency page instead of waiting.

consent.title: Confidentiality and consent
consent.body: Please read this before you send your request.
points: What you share is kept confidential and is seen only by the Foundation's authorised counselling staff.
Your request is stored separately from the public website and is never published.
Counselling is voluntary. You can stop at any point, and you can ask us to delete your information.
If a qualified professional believes you or a child is at serious risk of harm, they may need to involve someone who can help keep you safe. They will talk to you about this wherever possible.
The Foundation is not an emergency service and cannot respond outside working hours.
consent.checkbox: I have read the above and I would like to request counselling support.
consent.safeguardingLink: Read the full safeguarding and privacy notice
consent.required: Please confirm you have read the confidentiality notice before sending.

review.title: Check your request
review.body: Nothing has been sent yet. Please look over your answers — you can go back and change anything.

submitted.title: Your request has been sent
submitted.body: Thank you for reaching out. A qualified therapist will review your request and contact you the way you asked.
submitted.refHint: Write these down somewhere safe. Together they let you check your request without giving your name.
whatNext: A therapist reviews your request — usually within two working days.
We contact you using the method you chose, at a time that suits you.
If we agree a session, you'll get the date, time and place confirmed.
You can check the status yourself at any point using your reference and code.
submitted.urgentNote: If your situation changes and you need help sooner, please use the emergency page.

privacy.title: Privacy commitment
privacy.lede: How the Foundation handles what you tell us.

sections.title: The principle we work to
sections.body: Private counselling data must never be treated like ordinary website content. Counselling requests, case records, session notes, intake information, therapist notes, referral information and appointment details are held separately from everything published on this site, and no public visitor can reach them.

sections.title: What we collect when you request counselling
sections.body: A preferred name (which need not be your real one), an age range, the category that describes you, contact details of your choosing, a general reason for seeking support, your preferred language, and a preferred date and time. We ask a safety question so we know how urgently to respond.

sections.title: Who can see it
sections.body: Only authorised Foundation counselling staff. Administrative staff see what they need in order to arrange appointments — they do not have access to clinical notes. Volunteers, donors and website visitors never see any of it.

sections.title: How long we keep it
sections.body: Case records are retained for as long as the Foundation's professional and legal obligations require, then securely destroyed. You can ask us to delete your information at any time, and we will unless we are required to keep it.

sections.title: The app on your phone
sections.body: This site can be installed as an app. Public pages — articles, events, emergency contacts — are stored on your device so they load quickly and work with a poor connection. Counselling pages and anything you type into the private form are deliberately excluded from that offline storage.

sections.title: Your choices
sections.body: You can ask what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, ask us to delete it, or withdraw your consent to counselling at any point. None of these requests affect your ability to come back later.

safeguarding.title: Safeguarding commitment
safeguarding.lede: The Foundation supports women and, in some cases, minors. These are the principles our staff work to.
safeguarding.intro: Safeguarding is not a policy document that sits in a drawer. It shapes how the intake form is written, who can see a request, and what happens when someone tells us they are not safe.

sections.title: Child safeguarding
sections.body: Where a beneficiary is under 18, additional protections apply. Staff are trained to recognise risk and to respond in a way that keeps the young person informed and involved wherever possible.

sections.title: Consent
sections.body: Counselling is voluntary and consent is asked for explicitly, in plain language, before any request is submitted. Consent can be withdrawn at any time.

sections.title: Confidentiality and its limits
sections.body: What you share is confidential. The exception is where a qualified professional judges there is a serious risk of harm to you or to a child — then they may need to involve someone who can help keep you safe. Wherever possible this is discussed with you first.

sections.title: Disclosures
sections.body: Disclosures of abuse, domestic violence or sexual abuse are handled by qualified staff following a defined procedure. They are recorded in the confidential case record only, never in ordinary system logs.

sections.title: Risk of self-harm
sections.body: Where risk is identified, the therapist follows an agreed escalation route and works with the person on a safety plan appropriate to their situation.

sections.title: Emergency escalation
sections.body: Staff have a defined route for urgent situations, including verified emergency contacts and referral partners.

sections.title: Professional boundaries
sections.body: Counselling takes place within agreed sessions and agreed channels. Staff do not conduct counselling through personal accounts or outside the Foundation's systems.

sections.title: Referrals
sections.body: Where someone needs specialist care the Foundation does not provide, we refer them to an appropriate professional or organisation and follow up that the connection was made.

sections.title: Data protection
sections.body: Counselling data is stored separately, access is restricted by role, and every access is logged. See the privacy commitment for detail.

safeguarding.concernBody: If you are worried about how the Foundation has handled something, or about the conduct of anyone connected with us, please contact us. Concerns are taken seriously and looked into.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.lede: We want this platform to work for everyone who needs it.
accessibility.body: The site is built to modern accessibility practice: it can be used entirely by keyboard, meets contrast requirements, labels every form field, describes every image, and shows clear focus. If something here does not work for you, please tell us — we will fix it.
